aboutPage.h2: The brief is a hypothesis. The object is the answer.
aboutPage.label: About
aboutPage.lead: GESTALTUNG is an engineering studio and manufacturing platform based in Doha, Qatar. We work at the intersection of industrial design, mechanical engineering, and precision fabrication.
aboutPage.p1: We approach every project as an engineering problem — not an aesthetic exercise. Form is always the result of decisions made under constraints: materials, processes, tolerances, cost, and use. When those decisions are made with rigour, the result tends to look right.
aboutPage.p2: GESTALTUNG was founded to close the gap between the design studio and the factory floor. Too often, products are designed without understanding what they'll require to make, and manufactured without understanding what they were meant to be. We operate across both.
aboutPage.p3: Our studio handles concept development, engineering, and documentation. Our manufacturing network produces the parts. Our shop sells objects that came through the same process. One consistent standard, end to end.
aboutPage.pr1d: Every design problem has a set of constraints. Material cost, manufacturing process, assembly sequence, maintenance access, regulatory compliance. We start with the constraints and let the design follow.
aboutPage.pr2d: A concept that can't be communicated precisely is a concept that can't be built. We hold technical documentation to the same standard as the design itself — clear, complete, and unambiguous.
aboutPage.pr3d: A dimension without a tolerance is a wish. We define tolerances based on function, not convention, and we understand the manufacturing implications of every number we write down.
aboutPage.pr4d: Design and manufacturing are not separate disciplines in this studio. The same rigour that goes into the model goes into the drawing, the quote, the first article inspection, and the delivery. No handover gap.

faqPage.a1: Fill out the brief form on the Studio page. Describe the problem, your constraints, and any target processes or materials. We'll review your brief and respond within 24 hours with questions or a scope proposal.
faqPage.a10: General machining tolerance is ±0.1 mm unless specified. CNC 5-axis can achieve ±0.005 mm for critical features. Laser cutting is ±0.1 mm, FDM printing is ±0.2 mm. Tolerances must be explicitly called out on the drawing — we manufacture to what's documented.
faqPage.a11: Aluminium (6061, 7075, 5052), mild steel, stainless (304, 316), brass, copper, and engineering plastics (Nylon, Delrin, UHMWPE) for machining. Standard polymers (PLA, PETG, ABS, PA12) for 3D printing. Specialty materials on request — ask if you don't see what you need.
faqPage.a12: There's no minimum quantity. We produce single prototypes and production runs of thousands. Unit price varies with quantity — include your target run size in your quote request.
faqPage.a13: Yes: anodising (clear, black, colour), powder coating, brushing, bead blasting, electroplating, and painting. Specify the finish and any colour reference (RAL, Pantone) in your quote request.
faqPage.a14: Yes. First Article Inspection (FAI) reports and dimensional inspection with CMM are available on request. Specify required inspection documentation at quote stage so we can include it in scope and price.
faqPage.a15: Within Qatar: 1–2 business days. GCC countries: 3–5 business days. International: 7–14 business days depending on destination and customs. All orders ship with tracking.
faqPage.a16: Bank transfer (preferred for large orders), credit card via secure payment link, and local payment on collection in Doha. Invoices are issued in QAR. USD invoicing available on request.
faqPage.a17: Physical products may be returned within 14 days if unused and in original condition. Digital products are non-refundable once downloaded. Custom or made-to-order items cannot be returned unless faulty.
faqPage.a2: As much as you can give. Reference images, sketches, competitor products, size constraints, material preferences, and target manufacturing process all help. If you have nothing — that's fine too. We'll start with questions.
faqPage.a3: We deliver in whatever format the project requires: STEP, IGES, STL for 3D data; DXF or DWG for 2D; PDF for technical drawings; SolidWorks native files on request. Everything is documented and named to a consistent standard.
faqPage.a4: Yes. Many clients engage the studio for design and documentation only, then take files to their own manufacturers. We have no obligation to manufacture what we design.
faqPage.a5: Yes. Design review, DFM analysis, and drawing audits are common engagements. Send us the files and describe your concern — we'll assess and propose what's needed.
faqPage.a6: Yes. We work remotely with clients across the GCC and internationally. Design and engineering services are fully remote-compatible. Manufacturing and shipping logistics depend on location — contact us to discuss.
faqPage.a7: Studio projects are scoped and priced per engagement — we don't publish day rates because scope varies too much. Manufacturing is quoted per file, per process, based on geometry, material, quantity, and tolerance. You'll receive a written quote before any work begins.
faqPage.a8: Yes. We routinely sign mutual NDAs before reviewing client files. Send us your standard NDA or request ours — we'll execute before any technical information is exchanged.
faqPage.a9: STEP and IGES for 3D machining and printing. DXF or DWG for laser cutting and sheet metal. PDF technical drawings are required for toleranced features. STL is accepted for 3D printing only. Always include a drawing — models alone are insufficient for toleranced work.

home.lead: GESTALTUNG connects industrial design, precision manufacturing, and product commerce into one integrated system. From first sketch to delivered part — without the gaps.

home.s2desc: CNC machining, laser cutting, 3D printing, and sheet metal — parts made with measurable intent.
home.s3desc: Precision tools, fixtures, and designed objects ready to ship. Form follows function, always.

mfgPage.cncDesc: Precision milling and turning across aluminium, steel, brass, and engineering plastics. Full 5-axis for complex geometry.
mfgPage.formLead: Provide your CAD files, quantity, material preference, and any tolerance or surface finish requirements. We'll review and respond within 24 hours with a detailed quote and lead time.
mfgPage.label: 02 / Manufacturing
mfgPage.laserDesc: High-precision sheet profiling in mild steel, stainless, aluminium, and acrylic up to 25 mm thickness.
mfgPage.lead: Six manufacturing processes, one platform. Upload your files, specify your tolerances, and receive production-quality parts — tracked from first operation to final inspection.
mfgPage.mouldDesc: From soft-tool prototype runs to hardened production moulds. Material selection support for mechanical and aesthetic requirements.
mfgPage.printDesc: Rapid prototyping and end-use parts in standard and engineering-grade polymers. Multi-material and flexible options available.
mfgPage.sheetDesc: Complete sheet metal workflow — laser profiling, CNC bending, welding, and finishing in one coordinated process.
mfgPage.vacuumDesc: Small-batch production using silicone moulds cast from a master. Excellent for pre-production validation and small series.

studioPage.briefD: You describe the problem, constraints, and target. We ask the right questions to scope the work clearly.
studioPage.conceptD: Initial sketches and geometry exploration. We present two or three directions with a recommended path.
studioPage.d1: Form, ergonomics, material language, and product identity — from concept to refined 3D model.
studioPage.d2: Structural analysis, mechanism design, tolerance stack-ups, and design for manufacture review.
studioPage.d3: Parametric and surface modelling for complex geometries. Output in STEP, IGES, STL, or native formats.
studioPage.d4: ISO and ASME compliant 2D drawings, assembly documentation, and BOMs ready for production.
studioPage.d5: From CAD to physical prototype. FDM, SLA, and machined samples for form and function validation.
studioPage.d6: Optimising geometry, tolerances, and materials for the target process. Reducing cost without reducing quality.
studioPage.deliveryD: Final CAD files, technical drawings, and documentation handed over. Ready for manufacturing or tender.
studioPage.devD: Refined 3D model, structural review, and design for manufacture analysis. Iterative and transparent.
studioPage.formLead: The more context you give, the better we can scope and respond. Include any constraints, target processes, or materials you have in mind. Sketches and reference files are welcome.
